messages:
maya: Heads-up — we had a collision this morning where an automation batch and an engineer both updated the same flag scope and the console ended up showing a confusing state.
jon: ugh. what happened exactly?
maya: automation pushed a scope change (batch rollout -> 20%) at 09:12 and carla manually bumped to 50% at 09:13. The console showed 50% but the audit log only listed the automation change.
carla: i only saw the console state; the audit entry was missing so i assumed my change was the only one.
samir: that sounds like a merge/visibility bug. Are we doing last-write-wins on the API? or is it a blind patch that drops fields?
maya: API currently treats PATCH as a shallow merge but our console does a replace on the local view when you hit save — race wins in client.
jon: logs show automation used /v2/flags/patch with {scope: X} and the console used PUT with full object. so the PUT overwrote the audit pointer for "modified_by".
laura: from product POV we need a clear UX: show concurrent edits and surface diffs before commit. But also want low friction for fast ops.
carla: For large teams, optimistic concurrency would help — like ETag or a version number. Could we add a lightweight conflict response? 409 with the diff.
maya: +1. Also we need per-field audit: who changed 'scope' vs who changed 'description'. Right now audit is per-flag which hides multi-author edits.
ops-bot: ALERT: flag-change-surge detected 2025-10-06T09:12Z — 18 changes in 2 minutes (automation pipeline)
samir: ops-bot nailed it. Telemetry also didn't capture the "intent" (automation vs manual) cleanly — both show actor id but automation uses service account that isn't always surfaced in console filters.
jon: implementation idea: switch to three-way merge on server: (base, incoming, current). If incoming deviates from base and current also deviates => return 409 plus unified diff. If only incoming deviates => accept and return new version. This keeps PUT as strong write and PATCH as intended merge.
carla: and in the console, before PUT we can GET latest and show a tiny inline diff modal: "Automation changed X at 09:12, you changed Y at 09:13 — continue? [View diff] [Abort] [Merge locally]"
laura: we should require a small "change reason" for manual overrides that differ from active automation — helps audits and SRE blameless postmortems.
maya: operationally we also need a safe rollout backstop: when scope increases >10% and change origin = manual, prompt for a canary and apply at cohort-level rather than global.
samir: also quota impact — we had a few routes that depend on scope size for quota mapping; sudden increases can cause quota thrash. We need a config change webhook that hints affected routes.
jon: on the API side: proposal:

```
PATCH /v2/flags/:id
If-None-Match: "v123"  // optional
Body: { scope: { percentage: 50 } }

Responses:
200 { new_version: "v124", applied: true }
409 { current: {...}, base: {...}, diff: "..." }
```

and for PUT keep semantics but require If-Match header for safety.
carla: can we provide a dry-run param on console save? console could call `?dry_run=true` to surface diffs without committing.
maya: yes. And we should record the dry-run result in a transient telemetry bucket so we can see whether people are frequently hitting conflicts.
laura: product asks: will this add too much friction for quick fixes? we need a way to bypass with an extra confirmation for emergent ops.
samir: add an "emergency override" checkbox that requires 2FA or an ops acknowlegement; also logs the bypass reason and who approved.
jon: backlog tasks:
- server: implement three-way merge + 409 diff payload (api)
- console: surface diffs + dry-run + reason modal
- telemetry: add per-field audit, dry-run bucket, origin tags (automation vs user)
- routing: emit impacted route list on change webhooks (quota hints)
- ops: small runbook for emergency override + 2FA hook

carla: can we also add a small visual tag in console list for "recently automated change" so it's obvious who last touched it?
maya: yes, add microbadges and filter by origin.
ops-bot: NOTE: sched maintenance 2025-10-07 01:00-02:00 UTC — deploying flag-api change to staging first
jon: ok i'll pick up the server piece; samir can own telemetry + webhook hints; carla will do console UX changes; maya will draft runbook and docs.
laura: i'll write a short policy doc for manual overrides and change reasons.
carla: one more thing — tests: we need integration tests simulating concurrent automation + manual edit to prevent regressions.
jon: agree. will add test harness to pipeline (simulate 500 concurrent edits with mixed PUT/PATCH).
maya: thanks all. let's sync in the weekly eng-platform standup tomorrow and link the PRs.
carla: thx :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Reminder: create incident channel #flag-merge-none if you hit unexpected production divergence
